item.text:
The HVAC demand flexibility measures are **upgrades 24–28**. They differ in whether they adjust thermostats **during the peak** to shed load or **before the peak** to shift load, plus the temperature offset and preconditioning duration. [Official upgrade list](https://resstock.nlr.gov/datasets)

| Upgrade | Measure ID | Strategy | Thermostat offset | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **24** | `dr_001` | On-peak load shedding | 2°F | During the peak |
| **25** | `dr_002` | Pre-peak load shifting | 2°F | 4 hours before the peak |
| **26** | `dr_003` | On-peak load shedding | 4°F | During the peak |
| **27** | `dr_004` | Pre-peak load shifting | 4°F | 4 hours before the peak |
| **28** | `dr_005` | Pre-peak load shifting | 2°F | 1 hour before the peak |

The upgrade numbers and measure IDs are documented in the [2025 Release 1 README, pp. 13–14](https://oedi-data-lake.s3.amazonaws.com/nrel-pds-building-stock/end-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock/2025/resstock_amy2018_release_1/README_resstock_20251.pdf).

**Load shedding (24 and 26)** lowers the heating setpoint or raises the cooling setpoint during peak hours, allowing indoor temperatures to drift to reduce demand. Upgrade 26 uses a larger adjustment than 24.

**Load shifting (25, 27, and 28)** raises the heating setpoint or lowers the cooling setpoint beforehand to preheat or precool the home. Stored heat or cooling then reduces HVAC demand during the peak. Upgrade 27 uses a larger offset than 25; upgrade 28 shortens 25’s preconditioning period from four hours to one. These shifting scenarios do not also apply an on-peak thermostat offset. [HVAC Load Flexibility documentation, §§1.2 and 4.4](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/93846.pdf)

There is a **documentation discrepancy about shedding duration**: the November 2025 README describes a **one-hour** on-peak window for upgrades 24 and 26, while the March 2026 detailed measure report specifies **four hours** in its final scenario table. The strategy, offsets, and preconditioning durations agree across the documents.

For analysis, these profiles represent nearly daily dispatch to estimate technical potential. Annual energy savings should therefore not be used directly as estimates of a typical demand-response program. [Release README, p. 7](https://oedi-data-lake.s3.amazonaws.com/nrel-pds-building-stock/end-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock/2025/resstock_amy2018_release_1/README_resstock_20251.pdf)
